cases.translation: We are going to Orekhovo, to the park…
cases.explain: «В» expressing motion towards a destination takes the accusative; парк is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.translation: I just wanted to eat a bit of stewed fruit…
cases.explain: Eating or drinking only part of a substance puts it in the partitive genitive; a few masculine nouns like компот take the colloquial partitive ending -у instead of -а.
«С» in the sense of 'together with, accompanied by' governs the instrumental: с белым хлебом.

cases.sentence: Я стою на ___ и весь погружен в мысли о чувстве.
cases.translation: I am standing on the platform, entirely absorbed in thoughts about my feeling.
cases.explain: «На» answering «где?» (a static location, not direction) requires the prepositional case: на площадке.

cases.sentence: Они покаянно раскачивались на лавке, в такт моим ___.
cases.translation: They rocked penitently on the bench, in time with my accusations.
cases.explain: The phrase «в такт» ('in time with') governs the dative, so обвинения appears as обвинениям.

cases.sentence: Утащит, например, в аптеке флакон тройного ___.
cases.translation: He would swipe, say, a bottle of triple eau-de-cologne from the chemist's.
cases.explain: After a container word («флакон») the substance it holds stands in the genitive: флакон одеколона.
With the linking verb «был» the subject stays in the nominative — этот звук is what the sentence is about.

reading.ru: Едем в Орехово, в парк… в карусели покататься…
reading.question: Where does Mitrich say he and his grandson are travelling, and what for?
options: To Orekhovo, to the park, to ride the carousels
To Moscow, to buy white bread
To Yesino, to see a friend
reading.correct: To Orekhovo, to the park, to ride the carousels
reading.explain: Mitrich introduces himself and says they are going to the park in Orekhovo to ride the carousels.

reading.question: What name does the old man give, and what does he say about his grandson?
options: Mitrich — and the grandson is also called Mitrich
Mitrich — and the grandson has no name
Venichka — and the grandson is called Mitrich
Mitrich — and the boy is his son, not his grandson
reading.correct: Mitrich — and the grandson is also called Mitrich
reading.explain: He says he is called Mitrich and that his little grandson is a Mitrich too.

reading.question: How does the narrator describe the way the young Mitrich made sounds?
options: He did not speak but squealed, and through his left nostril
He spoke very quietly through his teeth
He spoke normally but too fast
reading.correct: He did not speak but squealed, and through his left nostril
reading.explain: The narrator says the boy squealed rather than spoke, producing the sound with his left nostril rather than his mouth.

reading.question: What excuse does Mitrich give for rummaging around the narrator's bench?
options: That he only wanted some stewed fruit with white bread
That he was looking for his grandson's ladle
That he wanted to sit down
That he was searching for his ticket
reading.correct: That he only wanted some stewed fruit with white bread
reading.explain: Mitrich insists twice that all he wanted was компот with white bread.

reading.ru: Дедушка – первый не вынес, и весь расплакался.
reading.question: Who breaks down in tears first under the narrator's questioning?
options: The grandfather, and then the grandson
The grandson, and then the grandfather
The man in the brown beret
reading.correct: The grandfather, and then the grandson
reading.explain: The grandfather cannot bear it and bursts into tears first, and the grandson follows.

reading.ru: У меня душа, как у троянского коня пузо, многое вместит.
reading.question: What does Venichka compare his own soul to?
options: The belly of the Trojan horse
reading.correct: The belly of the Trojan horse
reading.explain: He says his soul, like the belly of the Trojan horse, can hold a great deal — which is why he can forgive them.

reading.ru: Вы мне напоминаете одного старичка в Петушках.
reading.question: Who does Venichka say the two of them remind him of?
options: An old man in Petushki who drank only what he had stolen
The man in the brown beret
A conductor from the Kursk station
reading.correct: An old man in Petushki who drank only what he had stolen
reading.explain: He recalls an old man in Petushki who would steal a bottle of eau-de-cologne and drink it quietly in the station toilet.

reading.ru: Я тоже хочу с вами выпить.
reading.question: What does the newcomer say when he walks up behind the group?
options: That he also wants to drink with them
That they should be ashamed of themselves
That the train does not stop at Yesino
That he has lost his ticket
reading.correct: That he also wants to drink with them
reading.explain: The stranger comes up from behind and asks to join them in a drink.

reading.ru: То был черноусый, в жакетке и в коричневом берете.
reading.question: How is the newcomer described?
options: A black-moustached man in a jacket and a brown beret
A tall man in a railway uniform
A woman in a brown coat
An old man with a ladle
reading.correct: A black-moustached man in a jacket and a brown beret
reading.explain: He is introduced as черноусый, wearing a jacket and a brown beret.

reading.ru: И он поставил мне на лавочку бутылку столичной.
reading.question: How does the black-moustached man prove he is not a thief?
options: He puts down his own bottle of Stolichnaya on the bench
He pays the others for their drink
reading.correct: He puts down his own bottle of Stolichnaya on the bench
reading.explain: He says he does not steal from strangers and has come with his own — a bottle of Stolichnaya, which he sets on the bench.

reading.ru: Все пили, запрокинув головы, как пианисты…
reading.question: How does the chapter describe the way they all drank at the end?
options: With their heads thrown back, like pianists
In silence, without looking at each other
reading.correct: With their heads thrown back, like pianists
reading.explain: The closing lines have them drinking with heads thrown back like pianists, just as the announcement says the train will not stop at Yesino.

highlight.question: Which sentence says which part of his face the boy actually used to produce his speech?
sentences: Необычен был этот звук, и чертовски обидно, что я не могу его как следует передать.
И говорил не ртом, потому что рот его был вечно сощурен и начинался откуда-то сзади.
А говорил он левой ноздрей, и то с таким усилием, как будто левую ноздрю приподымал правой: «И-и-и-и, как мы быстро едем в Петушки, славные Петушки»… «И-и-и, какой пьяный дедушка, хороший дедушка»…
highlight.explain: Only the last sentence names the organ he spoke with — his left nostril, raised with the right one.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes how the old man in Petushki obtained and drank his eau-de-cologne?
sentences: Вы мне напоминаете одного старичка в Петушках.
Он – тоже, он пил на чужбинку, он пил только краденое: утащит, например, в аптеке флакон тройного одеколона, пойдет в туалет у вокзала и там тихонько выпьет.
Он называл это «пить на брудершафт», он был серьезно убежден, что это и есть «пить на брудершафт», он так и умер в своем заблуждении…
Значит, и вы решили – на брудершафт?..
highlight.explain: The second sentence sets out the whole routine: stealing the bottle from the chemist's and drinking it quietly in the station toilet.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows that the man in the beret has brought a drink of his own?
sentences: Я не ворую у незнакомых людей предметов первой необходимости.
highlight.explain: The last sentence is where he announces that he has come with his own bottle.

highlight.question: Which sentence reveals that the grandfather and grandson had their vessels ready long before they were offered a drink?
sentences: Дед и внук протянули мне свою посуду: они, оказывается, давно держали ее наготове, задолго до того, как я их поманил.
Дед вынул пустую четвертинку, я сразу ее признал.
А внучек – тот вынул даже целый ковш, и вынул откуда-то из-под лобка и диафрагмы…
highlight.explain: The second sentence notes that they had been holding their vessels ready long before he beckoned them.
